messages:
olivia: During a quick usability run, screen reader users said the eval scorecard keeps interrupting them when diffs stream. They hear an announcement for every item. We need a small design fix that ships fast. /cc @maria @ryan

maria: Agreed. Two constraints: 1) don't remove discoverability for SR users, 2) avoid repeated assertive announcements. Proposing a single offscreen live region + a visible "new results" mini-pill with count.

dev-bot: Accessibility scan: https://redwood.link/scan/abc flagged aria-live="assertive" per-item and programmatic focus moves.

ryan: Implementation idea: batch announcements and expose a keyboard "skip to new" link when there are unseen items. Minimal code:
```js
// batch announce + skip link toggle
let count = 0;let timer=null;
function onNewItem(){ count++; clearTimeout(timer);
 timer = setTimeout(()=>{ const ann=document.getElementById('sr-ann'); ann.textContent = `${count} new results`; document.getElementById('skip-new').hidden=false; count=0; },400); }
```

tara: UX copy nits: use "New results available" or "n new results". Avoid "Loading" — it implies work in progress. Visual pill should be focusable and keyboard-accessible.

qa-bot: Test cases: NVDA/Chrome, VoiceOver/Safari. Acceptance: max one polite announcement per burst, skip-link navigates to first new diff, visible counter updates. Automated test: simulate 10 items in quick succession and assert announcer updates once.

maria: Rollout: behind flag ff_batch_announcer, enable 5% hosted, monitor a11y logs and support. If any regression, rollback. I'll add microcopy and update the accessibility guide with keyboard instructions.

olivia: Thanks — let's keep this small and aim for a patch in the next release. I'll attach the user clip and file the ticket with owners. :raised_hands:
